corvus-venustus:study:1.title: A Fossil Thick-Billed Raven (Aves, Passeriformes: Corvidae) from the Lower Pleistocene of Crimea (Paleontological Journal, 2026)

facts.statement: The species was described by the author Zelenkov.
The fossil dates to the Pleistocene epoch.
The fossil was found in Crimea.
The species was formally named by Zelenkov in 2026.
The species was described by Zelenkov in 2026.
The species lived in the Early Pleistocene in the Taurida Cave deposits of the central Crimean peninsula.
facts.quote: from the Early Pleistocene () of the Taurida Cave deposits of the central Crimean peninsula.

facts.statement: Morphological analysis indicates the species is most similar to the modern thick-billed raven.
facts.quote: Morphological analysis places it most similar to the modern thick-billed raven (C. crassirostris).

facts.statement: This species represents the first record of African large-billed ravens in the region, suggesting a wider distribution for this group during the Early Pleistocene.
facts.quote: C. venustus represents the first record of the group containing the African large-billed ravens, which includes the thick-billed raven (C. crassirostris) and the white-necked raven (C. albicollis) from the region, indicating a wider distribution of this clade of ravens during the Early Pleistocene.
